sessions.name: Squat + Bench
sessions.desc: Progress productive workload with manageable effort. Bench gets priority for progression and recovery.
variationNotes: Maintain strength with reduced volume; no scheduled strength load escalation.
Seated leg curl (12–14 reps): Block 1: Hamstring hypertrophy. Choose initial load by RPE; aim to add reps before weight.

Heavy competition single; practise setup, pause and commands. RPE 8 governs the load: warm up, adjust the suggestion to the day, and log actual effort. If the first work set is at least one RPE above target, lower subsequent load 2.5–5%; if effort remains high, omit the last back-off and report the overshoot. No failed reps or extra max attempts.

Lat pulldown (8–10 reps): Vertical pulling and upper-back support. Keep this movement through the block; work within 8–10 reps at the target RPE. Choose the first working load by RPE; no load is borrowed from bench or another variation.

Triceps pushdown (10–12 reps): Triceps support without another heavy press. Keep this movement through the block; work within 10–12 reps at the target RPE. Choose the first working load by RPE; no load is borrowed from bench or another variation.

Reverse pec deck (12–15 reps): Rear-delt development. Keep this movement through the block; work within 12–15 reps at the target RPE. Choose the first working load by RPE; no load is borrowed from bench or another variation.

coachingInstructions.missedSession: Skip or move one session only if the next key session and recovery still fit. Do not stack missed quality, heavy work or long runs. After two missed sessions, illness or a week away, review the next block.
coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.
coachingInstructions.speedWork: Accelerate with stable technique. Reduce load or stop when speed or position deteriorates. An easy speed day is not permission to turn it into a heavy day.
coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.

coachingInstructions.missedSession: Skip or move one session only if the next key session and recovery still fit. Do not stack missed quality, heavy work or long runs. After two missed sessions, illness or a week away, review the next block.
coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.
coachingInstructions.speedWork: Accelerate with stable technique. Reduce load or stop when speed or position deteriorates. An easy speed day is not permission to turn it into a heavy day.
coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.

warnings: Goal pace is faster than the current performance estimate. Quality uses current fitness; reassess after comparable training or a recent race.
Long-run duration/history limits redistribute distance into supporting runs. Confirm those visits fit; do not silently add distance to the long run.
fuelling: Practise carbohydrate and fluid intake during long runs, rather than introducing it on race day. Start with familiar small portions totalling about 30 g carbohydrate/hour; progress towards 45–60 g/hour on longer rehearsals if tolerated.
Drink to conditions and thirst; record what you actually tolerate. Use the same foods/drinks in later race rehearsals.

coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.

fuelling: Practise carbohydrate and fluid intake during long runs, rather than introducing it on race day. Start with familiar small portions totalling about 30 g carbohydrate/hour; progress towards 45–60 g/hour on longer rehearsals if tolerated.

sessions.desc: Build repeatable technique and capacity. Support the main goal without unnecessary fatigue.
variationNotes: Strength exposure: demanding main work followed by a smaller volume dose. RPE 7.5 governs the load: warm up, adjust the suggestion to the day, and log actual effort. fuelling: Practise carbohydrate and fluid intake during long runs, rather than introducing it on race day. Start with familiar small portions totalling about 30 g carbohydrate/hour; progress towards 45–60 g/hour on longer rehearsals if tolerated.

coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.

fuelling: Practise carbohydrate and fluid intake during long runs, rather than introducing it on race day. Start with familiar small portions totalling about 30 g carbohydrate/hour; progress towards 45–60 g/hour on longer rehearsals if tolerated.
Drink to conditions and thirst; record what you actually tolerate. Use the same foods/drinks in later race rehearsals.

coachingInstructions.missedSession: Skip or move one session only if the next key session and recovery still fit. Do not stack missed quality, heavy work or long runs. After two missed sessions, illness or a week away, review the next block.
coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.
coachingInstructions.speedWork: Accelerate with stable technique. Reduce load or stop when speed or position deteriorates. An easy speed day is not permission to turn it into a heavy day.
coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.

fuelling: Practise carbohydrate and fluid intake during long runs, rather than introducing it on race day. Start with familiar small portions totalling about 30 g carbohydrate/hour; progress towards 45–60 g/hour on longer rehearsals if tolerated.
Drink to conditions and thirst; record what you actually tolerate. Use the same foods/drinks in later race rehearsals.

fuelling: Practise carbohydrate and fluid intake during long runs, rather than introducing it on race day. Start with familiar small portions totalling about 30 g carbohydrate/hour; progress towards 45–60 g/hour on longer rehearsals if tolerated.
Drink to conditions and thirst; record what you actually tolerate. Use the same foods/drinks in later race rehearsals.

coachingInstructions.missedSession: Skip or move one session only if the next key session and recovery still fit. Do not stack missed quality, heavy work or long runs. After two missed sessions, illness or a week away, review the next block.
coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.
coachingInstructions.speedWork: Accelerate with stable technique. Reduce load or stop when speed or position deteriorates. An easy speed day is not permission to turn it into a heavy day.
coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.

fuelling: Practise carbohydrate and fluid intake during long runs, rather than introducing it on race day. Start with familiar small portions totalling about 30 g carbohydrate/hour; progress towards 45–60 g/hour on longer rehearsals if tolerated.
Drink to conditions and thirst; record what you actually tolerate. Use the same foods/drinks in later race rehearsals.

limitations: Versioned coaching heuristics; tests do not establish individual competition readiness.
Existing approved programmes keep their saved policy until explicitly replaced.

replay.assumptions: Synthetic completion is a counterfactual, not predicted adaptation. Every optional exercise is completed in this stress scenario; it is not required baseline work. B selects loads by familiar technique/RPE instead of blindly accepting low suggestions; A one difficult day in week2; C repeated lower-body fatigue in weeks3–4. No pain in these main replays. coachingInstructions.missedSession: Skip or move one session only if the next key session and recovery still fit. Do not stack missed quality, heavy work or long runs. After two missed sessions, illness or a week away, review the next block.
coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.
coachingInstructions.speedWork: Accelerate with stable technique. Reduce load or stop when speed or position deteriorates. An easy speed day is not permission to turn it into a heavy day.
coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.

fuelling: Practise carbohydrate and fluid intake during long runs, rather than introducing it on race day. Start with familiar small portions totalling about 30 g carbohydrate/hour; progress towards 45–60 g/hour on longer rehearsals if tolerated.
Drink to conditions and thirst; record what you actually tolerate. Use the same foods/drinks in later race rehearsals.

fuelling: Practise carbohydrate and fluid intake during long runs, rather than introducing it on race day. Start with familiar small portions totalling about 30 g carbohydrate/hour; progress towards 45–60 g/hour on longer rehearsals if tolerated.
Drink to conditions and thirst; record what you actually tolerate. Use the same foods/drinks in later race rehearsals.

coachingInstructions.missedSession: Skip or move one session only if the next key session and recovery still fit. Do not stack missed quality, heavy work or long runs. After two missed sessions, illness or a week away, review the next block.
coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.
coachingInstructions.speedWork: Accelerate with stable technique. Reduce load or stop when speed or position deteriorates. An easy speed day is not permission to turn it into a heavy day.
coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.

fuelling: Practise carbohydrate and fluid intake during long runs, rather than introducing it on race day. Start with familiar small portions totalling about 30 g carbohydrate/hour; progress towards 45–60 g/hour on longer rehearsals if tolerated.
Drink to conditions and thirst; record what you actually tolerate. Use the same foods/drinks in later race rehearsals.

warnings: Recovery evidence remains unresolved: the affected lifts stay bounded until recovery is reviewed; later peak exposures are provisional.

coachingInstructions.missedSession: Skip or move one session only if the next key session and recovery still fit. Do not stack missed quality, heavy work or long runs. After two missed sessions, illness or a week away, review the next block.
coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.
coachingInstructions.speedWork: Accelerate with stable technique. Reduce load or stop when speed or position deteriorates. An easy speed day is not permission to turn it into a heavy day.
coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.

fuelling: Practise carbohydrate and fluid intake during long runs, rather than introducing it on race day. Start with familiar small portions totalling about 30 g carbohydrate/hour; progress towards 45–60 g/hour on longer rehearsals if tolerated.
Drink to conditions and thirst; record what you actually tolerate. Use the same foods/drinks in later race rehearsals.

Single-arm cable pushdown (10–12 reps): Triceps support without another heavy press. Keep this movement through the block; work within 10–12 reps at the target RPE. Choose the first working load by RPE; no load is borrowed from bench or another variation.

Rear-delt dumbbell fly (12–15 reps): Rear-delt development. Keep this movement through the block; work within 12–15 reps at the target RPE. Choose the first working load by RPE; no load is borrowed from bench or another variation.

coachingInstructions.missedSession: Skip or move one session only if the next key session and recovery still fit. Do not stack missed quality, heavy work or long runs. After two missed sessions, illness or a week away, review the next block.
coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.
coachingInstructions.speedWork: Accelerate with stable technique. Reduce load or stop when speed or position deteriorates. An easy speed day is not permission to turn it into a heavy day.
coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.

fuelling: Practise carbohydrate and fluid intake during long runs, rather than introducing it on race day. Start with familiar small portions totalling about 30 g carbohydrate/hour; progress towards 45–60 g/hour on longer rehearsals if tolerated.
Drink to conditions and thirst; record what you actually tolerate. Use the same foods/drinks in later race rehearsals.

limitations: Versioned coaching heuristics; tests do not establish individual competition readiness.
Existing approved programmes keep their saved policy until explicitly replaced.
